task_row_model.query: What is the recommended first-line oral antibiotic and duration for treating acute otitis media in adults?

documents.content: Academic review: Acute otitis media (AOM) in adults is an inflammatory infection of the middle ear frequently following upper respiratory viral infections and often involving Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae. Contemporary reviews identify amoxicillin as the preferred first-line oral antibiotic for uncomplicated AOM in adults, citing bactericidal activity and narrow spectrum compared with broader agents. The review contrasts AOM with otitis externa in terminology and briefly traces early antiseptic approaches in 19th-century medicine as historical context. It also speculates on rising antimicrobial resistance without providing prevalence numbers and notes that local susceptibility patterns may influence therapy choices.

Clinical practice reference entry: For adult patients with acute otitis media, recommended oral amoxicillin regimens are 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg twice daily; the usual recommended duration of therapy is seven days. These dosing options balance efficacy and adherence and are cited in clinical practice guidelines as first-line therapy for uncomplicated adult AOM. The entry restates that amoxicillin is preferred unless there is a documented penicillin allergy, in which case alternative agents are advised. The entry includes brief definitional boilerplate about dosing abbreviations and repeats guideline endorsement for emphasis.

Health news piece: Recent reports highlight that ear infections account for a notable fraction of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions, with pediatric cases driving much of the volume; adults make up a smaller share. Journalists cite one hospital's case study of a complex recurrent pediatric AOM patient who required tympanostomy tubes — an unrelated intervention — and note controversial commentary about overprescribing antibiotics. The article includes loose regional statistics on clinic visits, mentions doxycycline and macrolides as alternatives for people with penicillin allergy, and offers speculative opinion on whether telemedicine impacts diagnostic accuracy.

task_row_model.golden_answer: First-line oral antibiotic for acute otitis media in adults is amoxicillin. Recommended adult dosing is 500 mg orally every 8 hours or 875 mg twice daily, with the usual duration of therapy being seven days; this regimen is recommended by clinical practice guidelines.
